title: Inspection screens show only this organisation's and location's data
custom_preconds:
1. Two organisations/workplaces on the build under test, and a user who belongs to organisation A only.
  2. Inspection data belonging to organisation B: an inspection on an asset, a reference file on a template, and per-axle answers. Seed each in organisation B.
custom_steps:
1. As the organisation-A user, try to reach organisation B's inspection through the asset Inspections tab.
  2. Try to open organisation B's reference file and its per-axle answers by their addresses.
  3. Note for the tester: behind-the-scenes scoping is a developer/automated check. By hand, confirm only that no data belonging to organisation B (or another workplace) is ever shown to the organisation-A user.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The asset Inspections tab, reference files and per-axle answers are scoped to both organisation and workplace; a user in another organisation or workplace cannot read them.
  • Because the asset-history read deliberately crosses a customer boundary, the scoping is applied explicitly on each read rather than inherited from the customer join.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181 (Digital Inspections V2); Digital Inspections V2 Foundation Technical Implementation Plan (engineering tech plan .md, provided 2026-09-30), sections 1.3-1.4; read 30 Sep 2026. This behaviour is specified by the tech plan and is not covered by the PRD stories.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • NFR-005: “Every new read path is tenant-scoped. The reference-file and axle rows carry no tenant column of their own, so each read joins its aggregate root and applies both organisation and workplace.”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
